sentences.text: Based on later research, Megapiranha is estimated to have reached a length of 71 cm and a weight of 10 kg, with an estimated bite force ranging from 1,240 to 4,749 Newtons.

The preserved premaxilla is 6.9 cm long and features a rugose outer surface likely housing nerves and blood vessels, while the teeth feature a single crown shaped like an almost equilateral triangle arranged in inner and outer rows.
Megapiranha combines traits from basal serrasalmids with those of derived members, representing an intermediate form.
Tests on a replica suggest Megapiranha could penetrate bovine femurs, turtle shells, and catfish armor.
The genus Megapiranha was described by Cione and colleagues in 2009.
The holotype fragment was rediscovered by Alberto Luis Cione in the collection of the Museo de La Plata.
Researchers suggest that Megapiranha's dentition may not have been solely for carnivory but allowed it to consume a wide range of food sources.
Megapiranha belongs to the family Serrasalmidae and is classified as a transitional fossil within the subfamily Serrasalminae.
Megapiranha lived in Argentina during the Late Miocene, approximately 8 to 10 million years ago.
The time range for Megapiranha is recorded as the Tortonian to Zanclean stages, from 8 to 5 million years ago.
The hypothesis that Megapiranha fed on hard-shelled animals and larger mammals remains hypothetical due to a lack of fossil evidence like bite marks.
